bull.b: A proprietary proteomics platform gives Acrivon a differentiated framework for discovering precision oncology medicines and selecting patients more effectively. If validated in development, this approach could improve clinical trial efficiency, support targeted treatment strategies, and strengthen the company’s long-term competitive position.

Very low leverage and positive equity provide financial flexibility compared with a highly indebted development-stage company. This reduces fixed financing pressure and leaves more capacity to direct available resources toward clinical programs, although the benefit depends on controlling ongoing operating cash burn.

An active pipeline of investigational oncology candidates creates multiple potential avenues for future clinical and commercial progress rather than relying on a single program. Continued advancement in trials could expand the company’s strategic options and provide the basis for future partnership or product opportunities.

bear.b: A pre-revenue model means Acrivon has not yet demonstrated recurring demand or operating leverage from marketed products. Until a candidate is approved and commercialized, the company remains dependent on development progress and external financing rather than internally generated sales to fund operations.

Sustained operating and free-cash-flow deficits consume financial resources while the pipeline remains in development. Persistent burn can shorten the company’s funding runway, increase reliance on future capital raising, and limit the resources available for advancing several programs simultaneously.

An expanded equity incentive plan may help recruit and retain specialized biotechnology talent, but it also creates potential dilution for existing shareholders. Ongoing share-pool increases could raise the equity base over time and reduce each current holder’s ownership proportion if awards are issued.
